searchText: I think there is a number of useful features "dynamic initialization" provides. Maybe someone from solidity can complete this: - storage slots initialization, - immutables initialization, - creating sub-contracts, - calling other contracts. Maybe it is overkill when you only have static code to deploy. But I like that the initcode is ephemeral. And we should add and promote other ephemeral code use because it does not increase the state size. Hmmm. I hadn't thought of state size effect. Downside is that we can't amortize the cost of deployment-time validation across multiple calls. And without deployment-time validation we can't be rid of various runtime checks. But I guess the VM still has to be able to run pre-EOF unvalidated code, so that might not be an issue. For some of the others you mention, do you think we can find a way to handle them that doesn't require the ability to actually generate new code?
